gf_detail: If this record is the Ningyōchō 福そば, it is a firm no. The noodles are 生麺 made to the shop's own specification by an outside noodle maker and are not jūwari — wheat flour is in the noodle. Udon shares the same boiling water at the same counter. The kakiage and tempura are wheat-battered and deep-fried in a fryer that runs all service. The tsuyu the shop is actually famous for is built on ordinary Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat by default, and the house 辛味噌 is a miso paste with no gluten-free claim attached. No gluten-free item, no wheat-free handling, and a standing counter gives a kitchen no room to run a separate line.
vegan_detail: The tsuyu is a katsuo/dashi broth — it is the whole point of the shop — so even a plain kake soba is not vegan. The kakiage is vegetable but shares a fryer with prawn tempura, and the popular sides are 出汁巻き玉子 (egg) and 温玉. There is no plant-based tsuyu on offer.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yun (雲さん) — given only as a surname in the sources
chef_bio.origin: Xiamen, China; resident in Japan for over twenty years at the time of the 2020 profile
chef_bio.background: Written about the Ningyōchō 福そば, which is a real and well-documented shop — but the tie to this light record is a name match and nothing more, so read it as background on a candidate, not as this record's biography. Bungei Shunjū profiled the owner in February 2020 under the headline 「日本在住23年 中国人留学生が『日本そばの達人』になり、東京に名店を」: a Chinese student who came to Japan, worked in Japanese restaurants, and fell for soba by way of the tsuyu rather than the noodle. He runs a stand-up counter in Amazake-yokochō that opens before half past seven in the morning, and both the Bunshun piece and favy's 2020 write-up make the same point — that the usual excuses of a standing-soba shop are simply absent here. The noodle is a slightly thin 生麺 ordered to the shop's own specification so that it cooks fast without going slack; the kakiage is fried long and low with air worked into it with chopsticks, and the vegetables rotate with the season (spring chrysanthemum, prawn, lotus root, mushroom); a house-made 辛味噌 is offered as a seasoning. Prices in the 2020 piece ran ¥450–¥460 for tempura soba, ¥100 for a dashimaki, ¥300 for soba-shōchū cut with the hot broth; Tabelog's current budget band is under ¥999 and recent photographs show bowls up to ¥1,000. Cash only, no reservations, all seats non-smoking, standing counter.
chef_bio.philosophy: The broth carries the shop — simple, but with depth; no allowances made for the fact that customers eat standing up.
chef_bio.specialty: Kakiage and squid-tentacle tempura soba; cold soba in summer; dashimaki tamago; a shot of soba-shōchū cut with the hot soba-yu.

anecdotes.text: Bunshun's framing is that a Chinese student who had lived in Japan 23 years became a soba master and opened one of Tokyo's good shops — the hook of the piece is that he came to soba through the tsuyu, not the noodle.
The kakiage is fried at low temperature for a long time, with air pockets deliberately poked into it with chopsticks so it stays crisp under the broth.

Bungei Shunjū (Feb 2020) profiles the Chinese owner and the tsuyu. favy (Nov 2020) gives the owner's origin in Xiamen, the made-to-spec noodle, the kakiage method, the 2020 prices and the then-current 6:40 opening. Retty and several soba blogs corroborate the address and the standing-counter format. Nothing in any source places a 福そば in Shinsen or anywhere in Shibuya-ku.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Standing soba counter: soba and udon go into the same pot, and the tempura fryer runs continuously. Wheat is in the noodle itself, so there is nothing to protect.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shop's reputation rests on its tsuyu, built on ordinary Japanese soy sauce; no tamari or wheat-free soy is mentioned anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi in the tsuyu; the shared fryer handles prawn as well as vegetable kakiage; dashimaki and onsen-tamago are among the standard sides.

positives.text: Cheap, fast, all non-smoking, and open from 07:30 on weekdays — a genuinely easy breakfast or early-lunch stop if you have no dietary restriction.

cultural_comfort.level: Easy — but for the Ningyōchō shop, not for the Shinsen pin
cultural_comfort.note: The Ningyōchō 福そば is a stand-up counter: order at the ticket machine, eat standing, cash only, no reservations, no English menu mentioned. Foreigner-friendly in the sense that nobody has to talk, but there is no room to negotiate ingredients and no card payment. None of this can be attached to a Shinsen address, because no 福そば trades in Shinsen.

enrich_note: PROBABLE, NOT CONFIRMED — needs a human decision. Exactly one 福そば exists in Tokyo and it is at 中央区日本橋人形町1-16-3, a stand-up soba counter in Amazake-yokochō, roughly 7 km from this record's Shinsen pin. Two of the light record's three attributes contradict it: the shop is not in Shinsen, and it is not 手打ち (its noodles are made to spec by an outside noodle maker). Only the distinctive name matches. Legs run, all HTTP 200: Yahoo Japan "手打ちそば 福そば" / "福そば" 神泉; Yahoo Japan "福そば" 渋谷 OR 道玄坂 OR 円山町 そば; a full read of Tabelog's Shinsen-station soba area list (20 shops, no 福そば); plus direct fetches of Tabelog 13120777, Bungei Shunjū and favy for the Ningyōchō shop. Name, coordinates and loc_precise left untouched. Recommended action: either relocate this record to the verified Ningyōchō address above, or delete it — do not publish Ningyōchō detail against a Shinsen pin.

chef_bio.background: Could not be established, and the light record's 老舗 tag is contradicted by everything that was found. The 天ぷら 小島 that exists in Japan is 天ぷらとワイン 小島, a Nagoya business that started in 2015 in a four-tsubo unit inside Yanagibashi market and grew into a small tempura-and-wine chain — the opposite of an old Tokyo tempura house. Its one branch in this part of Tokyo, 天ぷらとワイン 小島 学芸大店 at 目黒区鷹番3-3-16 宮澤ビル1F, opened on 30 September 2023, closed at the end of February 2025, and the unit was taken over by ワンコイン割烹魚金 学芸大学 on 19 December 2025; Tabelog's page for it (13289483) is now marked 掲載保留中. Gakugeidaigaku is about 2.5 km from Ikejiri-Ōhashi and in Meguro-ku, so even that shop does not sit where this record points. The tempura restaurants that actually trade around Ikejiri-Ōhashi are 天ぷら たんご (129 m from the station), 天ぷら 筧 (191 m), 日日うどん, 旬彩なないろ and 夢吟坊 三宿本店 — none of them named 小島.
chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Four legs, all HTTP 200, all negative for a live 小島 tempura shop at this pin. (1) Yahoo Japan "天ぷら 小島" 東京 — the only real business is 天ぷらとワイン 小島 (tenpura-kojima.jp), Nagoya-founded. (2) Yahoo Japan 天ぷら 小島 池尻大橋 渋谷 — returns the Gakugeidaigaku branch and Tabelog's Ikejiri-Ōhashi tempura list, no 小島 at the station. (3) Yahoo Japan 天ぷら 小島 学芸大学 閉店 — 号外NET 目黒区 (26 Mar 2025) and a personal blog (1 Mar 2025) both report the Gakugeidaigaku branch shut at the end of February 2025; 区民ニュース gives its 30 Sep 2023 opening and the 目黒区鷹番3-3-16 address. (4) Tabelog's Ikejiri-Ōhashi tempura area list (tokyo/A1317/A131705/rstLst/tempura/) read in full — five shops, none named 小島.

cultural_comfort.note: Business could not be found. If a human wants a real tempura option at this pin, 天ぷら たんご and 天ぷら 筧 are both within 200 m of Ikejiri-Ōhashi station — but they are different businesses and would need their own records, not this one.

The only 小島 tempura business in this part of Tokyo was 天ぷらとワイン 小島 学芸大店 (目黒区鷹番3-3-16, a branch of a Nagoya tempura-and-wine chain, not a 老舗), which opened 30 Sep 2023 and CLOSED at the end of February 2025 — the unit is now ワンコイン割烹魚金 学芸大学, and Tabelog has the page 掲載保留中. chef_bio.background: Could not be established, and the record's own name is visibly corrupt: 个 is a simplified-Chinese character that does not occur in Japanese shop names, and searching it in isolation returns nothing but Chinese-language articles about university canteens. Two real businesses came closest and neither can carry this record. HITOSAJI is a curry shop in Ōsaki, Shinagawa-ku (Tabelog 13222005) — right reading, wrong cuisine, wrong side of the city. 渋谷食堂ひとしな / SHIBUYA SYOKUDO HITOSHINA at 渋谷区宇田川町33-1 グランド東京渋谷ビル2F (Tabelog 13289211) is a Shibuya teishoku restaurant whose name is one kana away, and it does serve daily set meals with olive-oil tempura and barley rice — but it is in Udagawachō off Center-gai, not Shinsen, and Tabelog has carried it as 長期休業中 (extended closure) since January 2024. Neither is close enough to publish, and a shop on long-term closure would in any case be the wrong thing to hand a traveller.
chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Five legs, all HTTP 200, all negative. (1) Yahoo Japan "个食堂" alone — nothing but Chinese-language canteen articles, confirming the character is not part of a Japanese shop name. (2) Yahoo Japan "个食堂" OR "ひとさじ" 定食 渋谷 神泉 — no matching business. (3) Yahoo Japan "ひとさじ" 食堂 東京 定食 — only incidental uses of ひとさじ as the ordinary word for 'a spoonful' in reviews. (4) Yahoo Japan site:tabelog.com ひとさじ 東京 — returns HITOSAJI (Ōsaki, curry, 13222005) and 創作麺 ひとすじ (Hōnanchō, ramen). (5) Yahoo Japan 食堂 ひとさじ 渋谷区 — returns 渋谷食堂ひとしな, whose Tabelog page was then fetched directly and shows the Udagawachō address and the 長期休業中 flag.

cultural_comfort.note: Business could not be found. The nearest name-alike, 渋谷食堂ひとしな in Udagawachō, has been on extended closure since January 2024 and should not be substituted in.
